notes: Checked robots.txt (no Claude-specific disallow) then fetched via curl_cffi (chrome124 impersonation) since direct requests/WebFetch got HTTP 403 (bot protection). Extracted the full site navigation JSON-LD (schema-top-menu-data, 255 SiteNavigationElement entries covering all 11 top-level nav sections: Living, Dining & Kitchen, Bedroom, Bath, Storage & Entryway, Office, Lighting, Rugs, Home Decor, Outdoor, Made for You) - zero Christmas/Halloween/Diwali/Easter/Valentine/Thanksgiving/New Year/Holi/Eid/holiday-named categories anywhere. The only seasonal-sounding item, a homepage promo tile 'Seasonal Favorites' (/catalog/home-decor/seasonal-favorites), resolves to a general editorial/entertaining page (og:description: 'Find ideas for dining rooms, bedrooms, home decor and gifts') with curated sets named 'Calm Escape', 'Comfort for All', 'Cozy Touches', 'Freshen Up', 'Gathering Place', 'Gift Ideas' - not tied to any specific holiday/festival, so it fails the seasonal-category test (rules sec4/sec6) and was excluded. Checked 'Gift Ideas' (/catalog/home-decor/gift-ideas) - explicitly all-occasion ('presents for the holidays, birthdays, corporate gifts or any occasion'), not holiday-specific, excluded per sec5. Probed direct URL guesses: /catalog/holiday and /catalog/home-decor/holiday (redirects to /clearance/home-decor/holiday) both return HTTP 200 but are soft-404 pages (og:title 'Information Not Found'). /holiday, /christmas, /catalog/home-decor/christmas, /catalog/home-decor/holiday-decor, /gift-guide, /holiday-shop all HTTP 404. Checked full static.xml sitemap (132 URLs) - no seasonal/holiday slugs. Internal site search (/search?q=christmas|halloween|holiday|diwali) is a client-rendered Next.js shell with no server-side query results (identical byte size across all queries, empty title) - not usable as proof either way, so relied on the exhaustive nav/sitemap check instead per the false-absence-search rule. Conclusion: Room & Board (modern furniture/home retailer) has no genuine seasonal/holiday product category in its taxonomy.
